glossary.Peripheral nerves: Nerves outside the brain and spinal cord that carry motor and sensory signals to the limbs and body.
glossary.Motor deficit: Loss of muscle strength or movement because the nerve to the muscle is damaged.
glossary.Sensory loss: Reduced or absent feeling in an area of skin.
glossary.Repetitive strain: Injury from repeating the same movement many times, such as typing.
glossary.Radial nerve: Nerve that straightens the elbow, wrist and fingers and supplies the back of the hand.
glossary.Humeral shaft: The long middle part of the humerus, the upper arm bone.
glossary.Crutch impingement: Pressure on the radial nerve in the armpit from leaning on crutches.
glossary.Median nerve: Nerve supplying finger flexors, thumb muscles and sensation to the thumb, index and middle fingers.
glossary.Median distribution: The skin area supplied by the median nerve: palm side of thumb, index, middle and half the ring finger.
glossary.Thumb abduction: Moving the thumb away from the palm, at right angles to it.
glossary.Thenar wasting: Shrinking of the muscle bulk at the base of the thumb.
glossary.Rheumatoid arthritis: Autoimmune joint inflammation that swells the wrist and can compress the median nerve.
glossary.Ulnar nerve: Nerve supplying most small hand muscles and feeling to the little finger side of the hand.
glossary.Intrinsic hand muscles: Small muscles inside the hand that control fine finger movements.
glossary.Radial deviation: Bending the wrist towards the thumb side.
glossary.Medial: Towards the midline of the body; in the hand, the little finger side.
glossary.Common fibular: Another name for the common peroneal nerve, which wraps around the fibular head.
glossary.Tibial condyle: The rounded upper end of the tibia that forms part of the knee joint.
glossary.Fibular head: The top of the fibula, just below the outside of the knee.
glossary.Knee dislocation: Displacement of the tibia from the femur, often damaging nerves and arteries.
glossary.Ankle eversion: Turning the sole of the foot outwards.
glossary.First web space: The skin between the big toe and second toe.
glossary.Intoxication: Being drunk or affected by drugs, so deep sleep allows prolonged nerve pressure.
glossary.Paralysis: Complete loss of the ability to move a muscle.
glossary.Radial head: The top end of the radius at the elbow.
glossary.Dermatomal: Following the area of skin supplied by one spinal nerve root.
glossary.L5 root lesion: Damage to the fifth lumbar nerve root, causing weak inversion and eversion plus foot drop.
glossary.Radiculopathy: Damage or compression of a spinal nerve root causing pain, numbness or weakness along its path.
glossary.Hip abduction: Moving the leg out to the side, away from the midline.
glossary.Posterior communicating artery aneurysm: A ballooned artery near the third nerve that presses on it, causing a painful palsy with a dilated pupil.
glossary.Shoulder girdle: The clavicle and scapula that attach the arm to the trunk.
glossary.Supraspinatus: Rotator cuff muscle that starts arm abduction, supplied by the suprascapular nerve.
glossary.Surgical neck of humerus: The narrow part just below the humeral head, a common fracture site near the axillary nerve.
glossary.Deltoid: The large shoulder muscle that lifts the arm, supplied by the axillary nerve.
glossary.Prodrome: Early symptoms before the main illness, such as diarrhoea before GBS.
glossary.Gastroenteritis: Infection of the gut causing diarrhoea and vomiting.
glossary.CSF protein: Protein level in the spinal fluid; raised with normal cell count in GBS.
glossary.Facial diplegia: Weakness of both sides of the face.
glossary.Autosomal dominant: Inheritance pattern where one faulty gene copy from one parent is enough to cause disease.
glossary.Hereditary: Passed down through families in the genes.
glossary.Lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh: A purely sensory nerve supplying skin over the outer thigh.
glossary.Splint: A rigid support that holds a joint still in a set position.
glossary.Steroid injection: Corticosteroid injected locally to reduce inflammation and swelling.
glossary.Decompression surgery: An operation to relieve pressure on a trapped nerve.
glossary.Nerve repair: Surgical stitching of the cut ends of a nerve back together.
glossary.Physiotherapy: Exercise-based treatment to restore strength and movement.
glossary.Conduction block: Failure of signals to pass a damaged segment of nerve, while the axon remains intact.
glossary.Axon: The long fibre of a nerve cell that carries electrical signals.
glossary.Transection: Complete cutting through of a structure.
glossary.Demyelination: Loss of the fatty myelin sheath that insulates nerves and speeds conduction.
glossary.Myelin: The fatty insulating sheath around nerve fibres that speeds signals.
glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Post-infectious: Starting after an infection has cleared, usually by an immune reaction.
glossary.CMT1A: The commonest Charcot-Marie-Tooth subtype, caused by PMP22 gene duplication.
glossary.Inguinal ligament: Band running from the hip bone to the pubic bone at the groin crease.
glossary.Entrapment: Squeezing of a nerve as it passes through a tight space.
